messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service `inference-autoscale` — capacity_exhaustion threshold breached in region us-west-2. queue_length=1348, avg_latency=2.3s. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-capacity. Pager: @oncall

pagerduty-bot: [INCIDENT] inference-autoscale — page delivered to Alex (on-call). Incident key: PD-89321.

Alex: acked. I'm on it — pinging infra and checking autoscaler status. Starting with recent scale events.

Samantha: seeing lots of pending pods in k8s for the past 6m, nodes not provisioning. Cloud API responses: 429 RateLimit and 403 QuotaExceeded intermittently.

Devon: can you paste the autoscaler logs? curious if there's a backoff loop.

Alex: past logs (tail):
```
2026-03-15T02:19:11Z autoscaler INFO: desired_nodes=40 current_nodes=12 backlog=1348
2026-03-15T02:19:14Z autoscaler WARN: cloud_api: failed_provision error=QuotaExceeded region=us-west-2
2026-03-15T02:19:20Z autoscaler ERROR: api rate limit, backoff=30s
2026-03-15T02:20:05Z autoscaler INFO: attempted_spinup node_group=spot-pool count=10 result=partial(3)
```

Maya: fwiw, spot capacity in us-west-2 is patchy right now — our fallback to on-demand should have triggered but I remember a recent change to prefer spot. If quota rules are strict, on-demand fallback might be blocked.

InfraOps: Confirmed — quota alert in cloud console around 02:17. There was a recent quota increase request still in review. Current usable quota < requested nodes for peak.

Devon: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) manually scale up a dedicated on-demand pool (temp), 2) reduce max-concurrency on router to slow ingress, 3) enable degraded-mode routing to smaller model variants. Which is fastest?

Alex: I'm doing (1) now — manual create/attach on-demand pool via infra tool. Command: 
```
infractl pools create --name emergency-on-demand --region us-west-2 --type on-demand --count 12 --labels=autoscale-fallback
```
Executing...

pagerduty-bot: Alex acknowledged the incident. Escalation policy will wait 5m for resolution before paging next rotation.

Samantha: while that runs we should throttle new requests at the edge. Pushing a temporary rate limit: `edgectl route update /v1/generate --qps 2000` to shed non-critical traffic.

Maya: also flip the routing policy to prefer compact quantized model (gpt-small-q4) for non-SLAs. Doing in Console -> Routes -> fallback-policy.

Alex: infractl responded: pool created (partial). 8 nodes provisioned, 4 still pending due to AZ capacity. I'm forcing pod rebinds to the new pool.

Devon: rebind command?

Alex: `kubectl annotate nodes ...` and restarting deployments with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-workers -n prod` on a subset to avoid thundering herd.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: acknowledgement recorded. Time to acknowledge: 00:00:22.

Samantha: after the restart, queue length dropped from 1348 -> 620 over 3m. Error rate on the API fell from 5.2% -> 2.1%. Latency temporarily spikes during rollout but then improves.

pagerduty-bot: Reassigning on-call to Maya (second-level) due to ongoing partial capacity.

Maya: taking point. Thanks Alex/Samantha. I'm monitoring scaling events and cloud console. Can we get a concrete customer impact statement? Product asked.

Devon: quick numbers from metrics: 12% of user requests saw >2s extra latency in last 15m; about 3% requests returned 503s during the spike window (02:16-02:24). Affected models: gpt-large and gpt-xl in us-west-2. No data exfiltration or model correctness issues.

Maya: noted. I'll prepare the incident banner and send the customer impact to support. Copy: "We experienced transient capacity exhaustion in us-west-2 causing elevated latency and brief 503s between 02:16–02:24 UTC for some generation requests. Engineers mitigated the issue; autoscaler fallbacks and on-demand pool spin-up restored capacity."

InfraOps: cloud quota increase approved for critical quota at 02:28 — new quota applied. Remaining pending nodes spun up; pool reached desired=12 at 02:30.

Alex: queue is now at 18, backlog cleared. CPU/GPU utilization normalized. Rolling metrics: latency back to baseline ~350ms.

Samantha: adding action items: 1) revert temporary rate limit once cold start safe, 2) remove emergency pool after traffic normalizes, 3) create follow-up ticket to improve autoscaler fallback logic to prioritize on-demand when spot fails or quota errors are returned.

Maya: handing over to Alex for post-incident writeup. I'll stay on the thread for 15m to confirm stability.

Alex: summary for postmortem starter: cause=quota_exhaustion + spot capacity shortfall; immediate mitigation=manual emergency on-demand pool + throttling + model fallback; impact=short window elevated latency & ~3% 503s; resolution=quota applied + nodes provisioned. Next steps: runbook update, alert refinement (differentiate quota vs provisioning), add cloud quota monitor to autoscaler.

Devon: creating GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/issues/5762 (Autoscaler: fallback & quota handling).

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved? Mark as resolved if no further action needed.

Alex: marking status: monitoring. If stable in 30m I'll resolve on PD.

Maya: handing off to next on-call (Devon) at 03:00 UTC. Good job team. :thumbsup:

Samantha: left small debug artifacts (temp pool: emergency-on-demand) — will cleanup after stable. Postmortem note: keep it blameless, we had a race between spot preference and quota availability.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now; please add notes to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-89321
